title: Your First CTE
story: A CTE (WITH ... AS) gives a query a name so the next query can read like a sentence.
goal: Using a CTE named totals with columns customer_id and spent (sum of qty*price over delivered orders), show customer name and spent, biggest first (columns name, spent).

tests.label: Hidden check on other data

hints: Write the CTE first and make sure it runs, then join it like a table.
totals has columns customer_id and spent.

WITH totals AS (SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(o.qty * p.price) AS spent FROM orders o JOIN products p ON p.id = o.product_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY o.customer_id) SELECT c.name, t.spent FROM totals t JOIN customers c ON c.id = t.customer_id ORDER BY t.spent DESC;
socratic: Why is it easier than one giant query?
Is the CTE stored in the database?
explain: In one sentence: what does this query do, and why does it need the a WITH clause?
solution: WITH totals AS (SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(o.qty * p.price) AS spent FROM orders o JOIN products p ON p.id = o.product_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY o.customer_id) SELECT c.name, t.spent FROM totals t JOIN customers c ON c.id = t.customer_id ORDER BY t.spent DESC;
alt: WITH totals AS (SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(o.qty * p.price) AS spent FROM orders o, products p WHERE p.id = o.product_id AND o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY o.customer_id) SELECT c.name, t.spent FROM customers c JOIN totals t ON t.customer_id = c.id ORDER BY t.spent DESC;
